app.title: Fisheye Canopy Analyzer
app.summary: A person uploads one upward-facing hemispherical photo. They fit a circular mask to the fisheye field of view by nudging its centre and radius against a live preview. Next they choose the colour channel, gamma, thresholding method, lens model and the zenith rings and azimuth sectors, then run the four-step pipeline. Tabs then show the masked image, the sky/canopy binary image, the ring-and-sector grid, and the canopy attributes derived from gap fraction (effective and true leaf area index, clumping, openness and leaf angle). From the results they can go back to the mask and run again.

task.text: Compute leaf area index, clumping, canopy openness and leaf angle from one fisheye canopy photo by masking it, thresholding sky from canopy, and inverting gap fraction over zenith rings.

data.text: A single circular fisheye photograph of a canopy, reduced to a binary sky/canopy image and a table of gap fractions per zenith ring and azimuth sector.
data.item: one hemispherical photo taken upward through a canopy

stage.text: analyzing canopy photos taken in the field to get canopy structure metrics

mechanism.text: A sidebar of numbered settings (mask, import, binarize, gap fraction) drives a live mask preview over the colour photo. After a run, four tabs show each pipeline stage as an image with summary numbers beside it, and the last tab shows the derived metrics and a full results table. An edit-mask button clears the results and brings the preview back, so the person can adjust and run again.

field.text: hemispherical photography for leaf area index and gap-fraction analysis in canopy ecology

workflow.name: compute summary metrics from one image through a staged, tunable pipeline

steps.here: Upload one fisheye photo (jpg, png, tif). This resets all state and sets the mask to the image centre with a default radius.

steps.step: mark the region of the image to analyse
steps.here: Arrow buttons move xc, yc and rc by a chosen pixel step, or the values are typed in. A live red circle over the photo shows the mask, and its coverage and any out-of-bounds warning appear beside it.

steps.step: set how the image is turned into a measurement
steps.here: Pick a channel or colour index, gamma and contrast stretch. Then choose global Otsu, zonal N/W/S/E Otsu or a manual threshold, the lens projection, the zenith range, the number of rings and the number of azimuth segments.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run Analysis goes through import → binarize → gap fraction → canopy attributes, with a spinner for each step.
Tabs show the masked grey image, the binary sky/canopy image with its thresholds and gap/canopy percentages, and the rings and sectors drawn over the binary image, each with its log.
Le, L, LX, DIFN, MTA and x appear as metric cards, LXG1/LXG2 as additional indices, and every value and setting in a transposed table.
Edit Mask & Re-run clears the results and brings the mask preview back, so the person can adjust and run again.

distinctive: The circular field of view has to be fitted by hand to the fisheye photo, with a live overlay, a pixel-step nudge control and a bounds check.
Thresholding can be done separately for each compass quadrant to cope with uneven sky lighting.
Pixels are binned by view zenith angle through a lens distortion model (equidistant or FC-E8) into rings × azimuth sectors.
Gap fraction is inverted with Beer–Lambert/Miller's formula, per ring for effective LAI and per sector for clumping-corrected LAI.
